reasons: Tests cover priority, near-miss selection, ground fallback, off-site clicks and hidden elements.
These tests were not run during this review.

terms.meaning: an invisible straight line from the camera through the mouse position, used to find what it hits
how many screen pixels away a click can be and still count as a hit on a thin item
one element of the facility, such as a breaker or a pole

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test tools and picking import
sections.what: Loads the test functions, three.js, the component type and the picking function.
sections.why: Needed for the tests to run.

sections.name: item
sections.title: Build a test item
sections.what: Makes a simple box at a set position and attaches its element id, as the real scene does.
sections.why: Gives the tests predictable objects to click.
sections.watch_out: Test items only set the shape name. Real elements carry many more fields.

sections.name: scene
sections.title: Bundle test items into lookup maps
sections.what: Packages the test items into the two lookup maps that the picker expects: one for the 3D groups and one for the element records.
sections.why: Mirrors the inputs the real scene passes to the picker.
sections.watch_out: Both maps must use the same ids, or the picker cannot match them.

sections.name: camera
sections.title: Fixed test camera
sections.what: Creates one camera above the origin looking down, with a 45 degree field of view.
sections.why: A fixed camera gives a predictable pixel tolerance for the near-miss test.
sections.watch_out: Moving this camera changes the expected tolerance and can break the near-miss test.

sections.name: rayDownAt
sections.title: Downward ray at a ground point
sections.what: Creates a ray that starts above a chosen ground position and points straight down, like a click from above.
sections.why: Simulates a simple click on the scene.
sections.watch_out: Only straight-down clicks are tested. Angled clicks are not.

sections.name: component picking
sections.title: Picking behaviour checks
sections.what: Four checks: equipment is chosen over the slab beneath it; a pole is chosen from 1.5 metres away; open ground returns the gravel and off-site clicks return nothing; a hidden element is ignored.
sections.why: These are the behaviours a user relies on when clicking.
sections.watch_out: The hidden test changes shared objects. If it fails part way, the breaker can stay hidden for later tests.

summary: Tests that mouse clicks in the 3D view select the right element: equipment over ground, thin poles from a short distance, and nothing when off site.
purpose: Check the picking rules in picking.ts using a small test scene.
why: Likely reason: picking rules are easy to break when tolerance or priority changes, and users notice quickly.
how: Builds a flat ground slab, a breaker and a pole, then shoots downward rays at chosen points and checks which element id comes back. Also checks that a hidden element is ignored.
inputs: A fixed test camera, downward rays, and the three test elements.
outputs: Pass or fail for each test.
risks: Only one camera and one screen height are tested. Real mouse drags and angled clicks are not tested.
debug: If a case fails, check the ray position in the test and the pixel tolerance in picking.ts. The test names say which rule is being checked.
